{{nihongo|'''Murahi Shrine'''|村檜神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimotsuke Province]].

{{commons category|Category:Murahi Shrine}}

'''Murahi Shrine''' ('''Murahi Jinja'''; むらひじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|qid=Q44843}}{{ill|Tochigi (city)|ar|توتشيغي (توتشيغي)|azb|توچیقی (شهر)|ca|Tochigi|ce|Тотиги (гӀала)|ceb|Tochigi (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Tochigi|eo|Toĉigi (urbo)|es|Tochigi (Tochigi)|fa|توچیگی (شهر)|fi|Tochigi|fr|Tochigi|gl|Tochigi|id|Tochigi, Tochigi|it|Tochigi|ja|栃木市|ko|도치기시|nl|Tochigi|no|Tochigi (Tochigi)|pl|Tochigi|pt|Tochigi (cidade)|ro|Tochigi|ru|Тотиги (город)|simple|Tochigi (city)|sv|Tochigi (stad)|sw|Tochigi, Tochigi|tg|Точиги|th|โทจิงิ (เมือง)|tl|Lungsod ng Tochigi|tr|Tochigi (şehir)|tt|Тотиги (шәһәр)|uk|Тотіґі (Тотіґі)|ur|توچیگی (شہر)|uz|Tochigi (shahar)|vi|Tochigi (thành phố)|war|Tochigi, Tochigi|zh|栃木市|zh_classical|栃木市|zh_min_nan|Totigi-chhī|zh_yue|栃木市|qid=Q44830}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a village shrine (gōsha). It claims the title of the Third Shrine of Shimotsuke Province.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, on {{ill|Taika (era)|de|Taika|es|Taika (era)|fa|تایکا (دوره)|fr|Ère Taika|hr|Taika (razdoblje)|ia|Taika|id|Taika|ja|大化|ka|ტაიკა|ko|다이카|nl|Taikaperiode|pl|Taika|ru|Тайка|sh|Taika (era)|simple|Taika (era)|sr|Таика|th|ไทกะ|tr|Taika|uk|Тайка|zh|大化 (日本)|zh_yue|大化 (年號)|qid=Q1077930}} 2 ({{ill|646|ab|646|af|646|als|646|am|646 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|646|ar|646|ary|646|ast|646|avk|646|az|646|azb|۶۴۶ (میلادی)|be|646|be_x_old|646|bg|646|bn|৬৪৬|bpy|মারি ৬৪৬|br|646|bs|646.|ca|646|cdo|646 nièng|ceb|646|ckb|٦٤٦|crh|646|cs|646|cv|646|cy|646|da|646|de|646|el|646|eml|646|eo|646|es|646|et|646|eu|646|fa|۶۴۶ (میلادی)|fi|646|fo|646|fr|646|fy|646|ga|646|gan|646年|gd|646|gl|646|he|646|hi|646|hr|646.|ht|646 (almanak jilyen)|hu|646|hy|646|id|646|io|646|it|646|ja|646年|jv|646|ka|646|kk|646 жыл|ko|646년|la|646|lb|646|lij|646|lmo|646|lt|646 m.|map_bms|646|mdf|646|mg|646|mhr|646|mk|646|mr|इ.स. ६४६|mrj|646 и|ms|646|mzn|۶۴۶|nah|646|nap|646|nds|646|nds_nl|646|new|सन् ६४६|nl|646|nn|646|no|646|nso|646|oc|646|or|୬୪୬|os|646-æм аз|pl|646|pnb|646|pt|646|qu|646|ro|646|ru|646 год|rue|646|sa|६४६|scn|646|sd|646ع|se|646|sh|646.|shn|646|si|646|sk|646|sl|646|sq|646|sr|646|su|646|sv|646|sw|646|tg|Соли 646|th|พ.ศ. 1189|tk|646|tl|646|tly|646|tr|646|tt|646 ел|uk|646|ur|646ء|uz|646|vec|646|vi|646|war|646|wuu|646年|xmf|646|zh|646年|zh_min_nan|646 nî|zh_yue|646年|qid=Q33285}}) {{ill|September 29 (Lunisolar)|cdo|9 nguŏk 29 hô̤ (nùng-lĭk)|ja|9月29日 (旧暦)|ko|음력 9월 29일|zh|九月廿九|zh_min_nan|9 goe̍h 29 ji̍t (kū-le̍k)|zh_yue|九月廿九|qid=Q840263|lt=September 29}}{{Sfn|Kazayama|1903|p=59}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|simple|Kumano Gongen|zh|熊野權現|qid=Q11568925|lt=the Kumano deity}} and {{ill|Sannō Gongen|Q11470054|qid=Q11470054|lt=the Hie deity}} ({{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|lt=Ōyamakui no Kami|Q10935105|qid=Q10935105}}) were invited and enshrined{{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}{{Sfn|Ishihara|1964|p=198}}. Ōyamakui no Kami is the deity of {{ill|Mount Hiei|Q748040|qid=Q748040}}, and its enshrinement here has been noted in connection with the nearby {{ill|Daiji-ji Temple|Q11435473|qid=Q11435473|lt=Onodera-san Daijiji Temple}}{{Sfn|Murakami|1967|p=121}}. The surrounding areas—{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Onodera}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamioka}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimo-oka}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mitani}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Niisato}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Furue}}, {{ill|Shimotsuhara|Q109369623|qid=Q109369623|lt=Shimotsuhara}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tatamioka}}, Komaba (now part of {{ill|Iwafunemachi Shizuka|Q11662858|qid=Q11662858|lt=Shizu}}), and {{ill|Iwafunemachi Washinosu|Q11676262|qid=Q11676262|lt=Washinosu}}—were collectively called the “Ten Villages of Onodera,” and the shrine is said to have been founded as their guardian shrine{{Sfn|Ishihara|1964|p=198}}.

In {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} 2 ({{ill|807|Q30016|qid=Q30016}}), the enshrined deity {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake no Mikoto}}, originally worshiped at the Hachiman Shrine of Onoguchi in {{ill|Minagawa|Q11580946|qid=Q11580946}}, which had been merged, was welcomed as the principal deity. Furthermore, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}} ({{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}}–{{ill|876|Q23815|qid=Q23815}}), the Hachiman deity that had been invited to Hachimanzawa in Minagawa Village was, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōkō|Q440518|qid=Q440518}} ({{ill|884|Q23895|qid=Q23895}}–{{ill|887|ab|887|af|887|am|887 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|887|ar|887|ary|887|ast|887|avk|887|az|887|azb|۸۸۷ (میلادی)|bcl|887|be|887|be_x_old|887|bg|887|bn|৮৮৭|bpy|মারি ৮৮৭|br|887|bs|887.|ca|887|cdo|887 nièng|ceb|887|ckb|٨٨٧|crh|887|cs|887|csb|887|cv|887|cy|887|da|887|de|887|el|887|eml|887|eo|887|es|887|et|887|eu|887|fa|۸۸۷ (میلادی)|fi|887|fo|887|fr|887|fy|887|ga|887|gan|887年|gd|887|gl|887|he|887|hi|887|hr|887.|ht|887 (almanak jilyen)|hu|887|hy|887|id|887|ilo|887|io|887|is|887|it|887|ja|887年|jv|887|ka|887|kaa|887|kk|887 жыл|ko|887년|la|887|lb|887|lij|887|lmo|887|lt|887 m.|lv|887. gads|map_bms|887|mdf|887|mg|887|mhr|887|mk|887|mr|इ.स. ८८७|mrj|887 и|ms|887|mzn|۸۸۷|nah|887|nap|887|nds|887|new|सन् ८८७|nl|887|nn|887|no|887|nrm|887|nso|887|oc|887|or|୮୮୭|os|887-æм аз|pl|887|pnb|887|pt|887|qu|887|ro|887|ru|887 год|rue|887|sa|८८७|sah|887|scn|887|sd|887ع|se|887|sh|887.|shn|887|si|887|sk|887|sl|887|smn|887|sq|887|sr|887|su|887|sv|887|sw|887|tg|Соли 887|th|พ.ศ. 1430|tk|887|tl|887|tly|887|tr|887|tt|887 ел|uk|887|ur|887ء|uz|887|vec|887|vi|887|vls|887|war|887|wuu|887年|xmf|887|zh|887年|zh_min_nan|887 nî|zh_yue|887年|qid=Q25010}}), merged into Murahi Shrine on the grounds that its original site was impure{{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}{{Sfn|Ishihara|1964|p=198}}.

In {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 2 ({{ill|939|Q23422|qid=Q23422}}), {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidesato|ca|Fujiwara no Hidesato|de|Fujiwara no Hidesato|fa|فوجیوارا نو هیده‌ساتو|fr|Fujiwara no Hidesato|ja|藤原秀郷|ko|후지와라노 히데사토|pt|Fujiwara no Hidesato|vi|Fujiwara no Hidesato|zh|藤原秀乡|qid=Q1136623}}, who went on to subdue {{ill|Taira no Masakado|cs|Masakado Taira|de|Taira no Masakado|es|Taira no Masakado|et|Taira Masakado|fa|تایرا نو ماساکادو|fr|Taira no Masakado|ja|平将門|ko|다이라노 마사카도|nl|Taira no Masakado|pt|Taira no Masakado|ru|Тайра-но Масакадо|sh|Taira no Masakado|sr|Таира но Масакадо|th|ไทระ โนะ มาซากาโดะ|uk|Тайра но Масакадо|zh|平將門|zh_classical|平將門|qid=Q1207652}}, is said to have prayed here for victory{{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}. There is also a theory that the shrine itself was founded by Hidesato. In Kōno Morihiro’s *Shimotsuke Kokushi*, it is stated that Hidesato, as lord of {{ill|Karasawa Castle|el|Κάστρο Καρασαβαγιάμα|fa|قلعه کاراساوا|fr|Château de Karasawayama|ja|唐沢山城|simple|Karasawa Castle|tl|Kastilyo ng Karasawa|zh|唐澤山城|qid=Q11418602}}, founded Murahi Shrine about one *ri* away to the northeast (the demon gate) to protect the castle{{Sfn|Kōno|1893|p=12}}{{Sfn|Suzuka|1902|p=294}}. Some sources describe this as a “reconstruction”{{Sfn|Tochigi Prefectural Education History Compilation Committee|1957|p=428}}.

From the medieval period onward, the shrine received devotion from the {{ill|Shimotsuke Onodera clan|ja|下野小野寺氏|qid=Q16141519}} and the {{ill|Sano clan|fa|خاندان سانو|it|Clan Sano|ja|佐野氏|zh|佐野氏|qid=Q11385058}}, lords of Karasawayama Castle{{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}. During the Edo period, it was also revered by merchants of Tochigi Town, where {{ill|Tochigi-juku|ja|栃木宿|qid=Q30926264}} was established{{Sfn|Higano|1966|p=50}}. In front of the shrine buildings stands a pair of Oribe lanterns dedicated in {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} 11, 12th month ({{ill|1726|ab|1726|af|1726|als|1726|am|1726 === Cultural Properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property (National Designation) ===
* '''Main Hall'''
: Built in {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853}} 2 ({{ill|1533|Q6443|qid=Q6443}}){{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}. According to some records, part of it was renovated in {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 21 ({{ill|1414|Q6179|qid=Q6179}}), and a major renovation was carried out in Tenbun 2 by {{ill|Sano Toyotsuna|Q11385105|qid=Q11385105}}, lord of {{ill|Sano Castle|Q11384983|qid=Q11384983}}{{Sfn|Murakami|1967|p=121}}. A carving of a {{ill|Melon|Q5881191|qid=Q5881191}}, said to have been embedded by the master carpenter {{ill|Hidari Jingorō|Q2668220|qid=Q2668220}} at the time of construction or major renovation, remains on the upper part of a side pillar on the southwest side of the hall{{Sfn|Kazayama|1903|p=59}}{{Sfn|Murakami|1967|p=121}}.
: It is a three-bay Kasuga-zukuri structure with a cypress-bark roof{{Sfn|Tochigi City Board of Education|2014|p=21}}{{Sfn|Iwafune Town Board of Education|1974|p=14}}. There is no distinction between the worship hall and the main hall{{Sfn|Murakami|1967|p=121}}. The {{ill|Tokyō (architecture)|Q7814068|qid=Q7814068|lt=to-gumi}} above the pillars supporting the front eaves are noted for unique features not seen in other shrine buildings of the mid-to-late Muromachi period, which was key to its cultural property designation{{Sfn|Murakami|1967|p=121}}.
: On {{ill|August 1|Q2788|qid=Q2788}}, {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 41), it was designated a Specially Protected Building under the then {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}} (equivalent to an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}} under the {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}})<ref>Home Ministry Notification No. 76 of August 1, Meiji 41 (see: [{{NDLDC|2950877}} National Diet Library Digital Collection])</ref>.

=== Subsidiary Shrines ===
Of the 11 subsidiary shrines, 8 are enshrined together in the subordinate shrine building of Nishinomiya Shrine. Orihime Shrine was destroyed by fire, and Itsukushima Shrine collapsed and has not been rebuilt.
* Nishinomiya Shrine
* Sumiyoshi Shrine
* Raiden Shrine / Atago Shrine

=== Access ===
* 15 minutes by car from {{ill|Iwafune Station|Q11475586|qid=Q11475586}} on the {{ill|Ryōmō Line|Q253391|qid=Q253391|lt=JR Ryōmō Line}}
* About 25 minutes by car from {{ill|Sano-Fujioka interchange|Q10885981|qid=Q10885981|lt=Sano-Fujioka I.C.}} on the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|Q428428|qid=Q428428}}
* 40 minutes from Tochigi Station on the JR Ryōmō Line / {{ill|Tōbu Nikkō Line|Q845954|qid=Q845954}} via the Tochigi City Fureai Bus Minagawa Hinokuchi Line bound for “Yurarakukan”
** Get off at “Murahi Shrine Entrance” bus stop, 5-minute walk (few services)
** Get off at “Eda Clinic-mae” bus stop, 20-minute walk
